issue: téwe-kʷe bʰréh₂term̥ mē stundté: singular 'your' (téwe) addressed to the plural offspring (2pl verbs ph₂sté, stundté, ḱléwsete); 2pl enclitic wos expected
h₁íh₂ h₁widʰéwh₂n̥s bʰúHt: h₁widʰéwh₂n̥s is acc. pl.; the predicate of 'became' must be nom. sg. h₁widʰéwh₂. Also 'sat by the fire' has no word for fire in the PIE (h₁ésyo pótnih₂ sédyet)

later e/o-grade scholarly-style fable fragment: eweket lacks the labiovelar of *wekʷ- (expect (e)wekʷet / ewewkʷet) though ḱ/ǵʰ are marked; ḱerd for the nom.-acc. ḱḗr; non-laryngeal notation (owis, eḱwons) is a convention choice
h₃rēǵés-kʷe gʰóstins: 'enemy' for gʰóstis is a Latin-only shift (elsewhere 'guest/stranger'; used as 'guest' in b093d5d2); otherwise sound
h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁éḱwōs HéHḱewes h₁ésmi: h₁ésmi is 1sg 'I am'; plural subject 'his horses' needs 3pl h₁sénti; minor: HéHḱewes accent (adjective is suffix-accented, expect HeHḱéwes)
h₃rēǵi (loc.) carries no accent; voc. h₃réǵ has short e although the root noun is lengthened-grade throughout (h₃rḗǵs, h₃rēǵés), expect h₃rḗǵ
tóh₁ mē h₁opéyōh₂ 'I shall not give them': mē is prohibitive/volitive; a negative statement (future-subjunctive refusal) wants ne

h₂nḗr m̥ǵh₂éy táwrōy h₁ésti 'the great bull has force': h₂nḗr is the root noun 'man'; the 'force' sense belongs to derivatives (*h₂nértom, Skt sūnára-), so the line most naturally reads 'the great bull has a man'
n̥ptéy (dat. of népōts): the weak stem is nept- (Skt náptre, Av. naptō), not zero-grade n̥pt-; expect neptéy
téwe swéḱuroybʰos ḱléwse: swéḱuroybʰos is dat./abl. PLURAL but the English and the following h₁ésyo ('his fire') require singular 'your father-in-law' (swéḱurōy or acc. swéḱurom)
h₂néres kʷékʷlōy gʷṓs yéwgt: 3sg yéwgt with plural subject h₂néres; 3pl (yugént) required

eḱwos is nom. sg., subject of a 3pl verb needs eḱwōs; wewekur lacks kʷ and uses the Sanskrit -ur ending (expect wewokʷr̥/-ēr); ḱludʰe for imperative ḱludʰi; ǵʰm̥on for nom. ǵʰm̥ō; kʷr̥neti for the nu-present kʷr̥néwti
dual nom. bʰréh₂terh₁, gʷénh₂h₁: consonant-stem nom.-acc. du. is handbook *-h₁e (Gk -ε), not bare -h₁; rest sound

ǵónh₁oh₁-kʷe bʰuHyéti 'and the offspring grows': ǵónh₁oh₁ is nom. du./ins. sg.; subject of a 3sg verb must be nom. sg. ǵónh₁os; also ǵeǵénh₁eti perfect subjunctive built on e-grade, perfect strong stem is o-grade (ǵeǵónh₁eti)

dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁: consonant-stem dual should end in *-h₁e; otherwise well formed (dusḱléwēs is a fine compound though not in the lexicon); minor: fem. subject h₁yéh₂ ... séh₂ with masc. predicate wĺ̥kʷos (wĺ̥kʷih₂ would agree, though a masc. metaphor is tolerable)
no error vs its own convention: Schleicher 1868 original verbatim (pre-laryngeal, Sanskrit-style a-vocalism); not corpus-grade modern PIE, keep only if tagged historical
ǵn̥h₁téy 'at birth': -éy is the i-stem dative; the locative is -ēy (ǵn̥h₁tḗy) per the stated i-stem convention; the engine table labels the -éy form LOC.SG
dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁: consonant-stem nom. du. should be *-h₁e; rest sound (good dual agreement, swóm reflexive)
mélit nos nos h₃éngʷn̥-kʷe: doubled enclitic nos nos; the second stands conjunct-initially where an enclitic cannot (expect mélit nos h₃éngʷn̥-kʷe)
